basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 7.' and it opens 'Vers. 7. Divisit in duas turmas. Non, ut quidam putant, in tres, sed in duas turmas'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 7. Divisit in duas turmas. Non, ut quidam putant, in tres, sed in duas turmas populum. Prima | turma duarum ancillarum Zelphae et Balae cum filiis suis. Secunda turma fuit Liae et Rachelis et eorum qui cum eis erant. Sed quaeri potest hoc loco, cum Deus promisisset Jacob auxilium suum dicens: Noli timere, ego tecum sum, et multiplicabo, cur timuerit et providerit saluti suae, et non potius se Deo commiserit custodiendum? Sed hoc monemur exemplo ne Deum tentemus, dum habemus quod pro salute nostra faciamus. Denique et Jacob, quamvis pro se sibi providerit, audiamus tamen quid orans dixerit.
